payout_quote: Typically, we recommend you pay participants at least £9.00 / $12.00 per hour, while the minimum pay allowed is £6.00 / $8.00 per hour. (prolific.com/pricing) ... After your first 4 cashouts, payments are instantly transferred to your PayPal. You'll always receive cash, never gift cards or points. Once you've earned at least $6/£6, you can cash out directly from your Prolific account. (prolific.com/participants FAQ)
timing: Each study shows its pay before you accept; studies typically run 2-30 minutes; cash out to PayPal once your balance hits $6/£6 (instant after your first 4 cashouts)
eligibility: 18+; complete Prolific's identity verification (Protocol checks) and profile; studies matched to your demographics; availability varies by profile and academic calendar
steps: Create a Prolific participant account and pass identity verification
Complete your full 'About You' profile so studies match you
Accept studies from your dashboard - each shows exact pay and time before you start
Complete the study carefully (attention checks; rejections hurt your approval rate)
Cash out to PayPal once your balance reaches $6/£6
catches: Study volume is NOT guaranteed - your demographics and the academic calendar (Sep-May is busiest) control how many studies you get; some weeks there is little available
There can be a waitlist to join as a participant
Failed attention checks or rushed answers get submissions rejected, which lowers your approval rate and future study flow
PayPal is the only cash-out method
First 4 cashouts are processed manually before instant cashouts unlock
biggest_catch: Prolific enforces a real $8/hour minimum - but study volume is never guaranteed. Your demographics decide how many studies you see, and slow weeks pay $0 no matter the minimum.

maximize: Fill out your entire 'About You' profile on day one - Prolific's own FAQ says eligibility filters tailor tasks to your profile, so a complete profile is literally how you get more studies. Check your dashboard regularly and sort available studies by reward-to-time ratio; slots fill fast. Never rush: one rejected submission for failed attention checks costs more in future study flow than the minutes you saved.
